facts.text: ISO 12100, ISO 13849, IEC 62061 and IEC 61508 form a general machine-safety toolkit: ISO 12100 addresses risk assessment and reduction, ISO 13849 and IEC 62061 address machinery control-system safety, and IEC 61508 is the parent standard for electronic safety systems across industries.
facts.quote: These four standards form the general toolkit for making any machine safe: ISO 12100 for assessing and reducing risk, ISO 13849 and IEC 62061 for the safety of control systems on machinery, and IEC 61508 as the parent standard for electronic safety systems in every industry.

facts.text: ISO 12100 is the basic type-A safety-of-machinery standard and specifies identifying hazards, estimating and evaluating risk, and reducing risk first by design, then safeguards, then information for use.
facts.quote: ISO 12100 is the basic ("type-A") safety-of-machinery standard: identify hazards, estimate and evaluate risk, reduce it first by design, then by safeguards, then by information for use.

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 is a type-C machine-specific standard under ISO 12100.
facts.quote: Machine-specific standards hang from it; ISO 21815-3 is "a type-C standard under ISO 12100" [Chapter 3].

facts.text: ISO 13849-1:2023, edition 4, is the generic machinery method for safety-related parts of control systems, including software, using the Performance Level (PL) scale.
facts.quote: ISO 13849-1:2023 (edition 4) is the generic machinery method for safety-related parts of control systems, including software, using the Performance Level (PL) scale.

facts.text: ISO 13849 does not itself assign the Performance Level required for the collision function. ISO 19014 is the sector framework for ISO 6165 machines, while ISO 13849 remains relevant for generically developed subsystems or machines outside the earth-moving scope.
facts.quote: It "does not itself assign the performance level required for this collision function"; for ISO 6165 machines ISO 19014 is the sector framework, but ISO 13849 stays relevant for subsystems developed generically or machines outside the earth-moving scope [Chapter 3].

facts.text: ISO 13849-2:2012 covers validation and lists simulation and software simulation of faults among validation methods.
facts.quote: ISO 13849-2:2012 covers validation and lists simulation among validation methods and "software simulation of faults"

facts.text: A draft of ISO 13849-2 edition 3 was issued in 2026.
facts.quote: a draft of edition 3 was issued in 2026 [Chapter 12].

facts.text: IEC 62061:2021, from the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), is the parallel machinery standard using the Safety Integrity Level (SIL) scale; the booklet lists the standard as current but not reviewed.
facts.quote: IEC 62061:2021, from the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), is the parallel machinery standard on the Safety Integrity Level (SIL) scale; the booklet lists it as current but not reviewed [Chapter 12].

facts.text: IEC 61508 is a seven-part parent standard for electrical, electronic and programmable safety systems in any industry; ISO 26262 for cars, ISO 13849 and IEC 62061 for machinery, and ISO 25119 for agriculture descend from IEC 61508.
facts.quote: IEC 61508 is the parent: a seven-part standard for electrical, electronic and programmable safety systems in any industry, from which ISO 26262 (cars), ISO 13849 and IEC 62061 (machinery) and ISO 25119 (agriculture) descend.

facts.text: IEC 61508-3:2010 defines software tool classes T1 to T3, which the booklet uses as a reference for how much qualification a simulator or other tool needs when its output is relied on.
facts.quote: IEC 61508-3:2010 defines software tool classes T1 to T3, a reference for how much a tool such as a simulator must be qualified when its output is relied on [Chapter 12].

facts.text: IEC 61508's proven-in-use route allows a reused element to receive credit from field history under strict conditions and demands higher confidence than the comparable ISO 26262 clause.
facts.quote: Its "proven in use" route lets a reused element claim credit from field history under strict conditions, with higher confidence demanded than the comparable ISO 26262 clause [Chapter 10].

facts.text: The booklet did not verify in detail either the IEC 61508 software-tool-class provisions or the IEC 61508 proven-in-use route.
The booklet's safety-case skeleton maps the intervention chain to ISO 13849 or IEC 62061 where ISO 19014 does not reach.
facts.quote: The booklet's safety-case skeleton maps the intervention chain to ISO 13849 or IEC 62061 where ISO 19014 does not reach

facts.text: The collision-mitigation intervention path needs a Performance Level or integrity assignment plus fault testing.
facts.quote: the intervention path needs a performance-level or integrity assignment plus fault testing [Chapters 1, 9].

facts.text: When simulation results become safety evidence, simulator errors can hide defects; tool qualification addresses that risk.
facts.quote: If simulation results become safety evidence, the simulator is a tool whose errors can hide defects, which is what tool qualification addresses [Chapter 13].

facts.text: The warning system's field history does not transfer to the braking function as proven-in-use evidence because adding braking changes the item.
facts.quote: The warning system's field history does not transfer to the braking function as "proven in use", because adding braking changes the item [Chapter 10].
